name: Archer IRM
tagline: Enterprise integrated risk management: risk registers, control libraries, assessments, policy workflow and audit trails across a whole org.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Archer is sold as enterprise licensing with no public list price.

verdictSummary: Archer is not an app, it is a configurable platform that a GRC team lives inside for a decade. The part an agent can reproduce in an afternoon is the data model: risks, controls, assessments, findings, owners, due dates. The part it cannot reproduce is the content and the paper trail: mapped control frameworks, regulatory taxonomies, questionnaire libraries, immutable audit logs, segregation of duties, SSO plus granular field-level permissions, and the fact that an external auditor already knows how to read Archer output. If you are one person tracking risks for a small company, a personal register genuinely beats a spreadsheet and you should build it. If you are producing evidence that will be challenged, the platform is the point.
coreLoopDIY: A local risk and control register with owners, scored risks, control mappings, periodic assessment campaigns and an append-only change log, rendered as a web app over SQLite.
requirements: Your own control framework content, nothing is bundled
Somewhere private to host it if more than one person needs access
whatYouLose: Pre-built framework and regulation content: ISO 27001, NIST, SOC 2, PCI, sector regulations, plus the crosswalks between them
Defensible audit trail: append-only logs, e-signature style attestations, evidence retention that survives a regulator asking who changed what in 2023
Role separation and enterprise SSO, so first line, second line and audit cannot see or edit each other's fields
Workflow at scale: assessment campaigns to hundreds of control owners, reminders, escalations, exception approvals
Connectors into ITSM, HR, asset and vulnerability systems that keep the register from going stale
moatNotes: GRC buyers are not buying features, they are buying something an auditor accepts without argument, and something that keeps accepting it after the GRC lead leaves.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the output has to hold up in front of someone adversarial. A risk register you wrote yourself is fine until an auditor, a regulator or a customer's security team asks for evidence of control testing over a period, with dates, owners, approvals and an untampered history. Archer carries the framework content, the workflow to collect attestations from hundreds of people who do not care, and the institutional familiarity that means nobody has to explain the tool. Add the configuration investment already sunk into it, and switching looks worse than renewing even to people who dislike it.
notes: A risk register is a weekend; a defensible one is not. The moat is bundled framework content plus an audit trail that an external auditor already trusts.
prompt:
Build a single-user, self-hosted risk and control register. No cloud, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLModel over SQLite, Jinja2 templates, plain HTML with htmx for interactions, no JS build step, no CSS framework beyond a small hand written stylesheet. Run with uvicorn. Everything in one repo, started by `make dev`.

Data model:
- Risk: title, description, category, owner, inherent likelihood 1-5, inherent impact 1-5, residual likelihood, residual impact, treatment (accept, mitigate, transfer, avoid), status, review_due date.
- Control: ref, title, description, owner, type (preventive, detective, corrective), frequency, last_tested date.
- RiskControl: many to many link with an effectiveness note.
- Assessment: a dated campaign holding Responses, one per control, with result (effective, partially effective, ineffective, not tested), evidence note and a file attachment stored on local disk.
- ChangeLog: append only rows capturing table, record id, field, old value, new value, timestamp. Writes happen in the same transaction as the edit. Never expose a delete or update path for this table.

Screens:
- Dashboard: counts by status, a 5x5 heat map of residual risk rendered as an HTML table with colour classes, and a list of reviews overdue today.
- Risk list with filters by owner, category, status; risk detail with linked controls and full change history.
- Control list and detail with test history.
- Assessment view: create a campaign, auto create one response row per in-scope control, mark results, see completion percentage.
- Import and export: CSV in and out for risks and controls, plus a JSON full backup endpoint.

Explicitly out of scope: multi user auth, SSO, email reminders, approval workflow, any bundled control framework content, regulatory crosswalks. Ship an empty database and a `seed_example.py` with five fake risks so the UI is not blank.

Secrets, if any ever appear, live in .env read via pydantic settings. Include a README stating plainly that this is a personal tracking tool and not an auditable system of record.
